recent_posts.title: Startups have an 'age of consent' problem
Y Combinator's culture shift from merit to trend-chasing
recent_posts.summary: A critical opinion piece examining the perceived decline of Y Combinator under Gary Tan's leadership. The author argues that YC has shifted from its original merit-based, founder-focused philosophy to chasing AI trends, funding unqualified or dishonest founders, and fostering a culture of silence where criticism is dismissed as hating. Key concerns include YC using its platform to promote Gary Tan's personal GStack project over portfolio companies, blocking critics on social media, dismissing legitimate feedback, the Delve fraud scandal, and inflated revenue expectations pushing founders toward shady behavior. The author contrasts the current YC with Paul Graham's original vision and expresses concern about low-quality founders being entrusted with building AI systems.

recent_posts.title: Vercel, Lovable, and Notion security incidents expose SaaS vulnerabilities
recent_posts.summary: A wave of security incidents is hitting major SaaS platforms. Vercel was breached after a third-party tool (contacts.ai) used by an employee was compromised, allowing attackers to access Google Workspace credentials and environment variables. The breach chain connects to Delvé, a YC-backed compliance company accused of faking SOC 2 audits. Lovable exposed user codebases, database credentials, and AI chat histories to any free account — a bug reported 48 days prior that went unaddressed. Notion has a years-old vulnerability leaking editor email addresses from public pages, reported in 2022 and still unpatched. Both Lovable and Notion were previously showcased as Delvé compliance customers. The author argues SaaS security is deteriorating as AI models make exploitation easier, predicting more breaches among the ~500 companies allegedly covered by Delvé's rubber-stamped audits.

recent_posts.title: Satirical sketch about a shoe company pivoting to GPUs
recent_posts.summary: A satirical comedy sketch about a shoe company pivoting to GPUs after selling its inventory and IP for $40M, then raising another $50M by adding 'GPU' to a YC pitch deck. The humor centers on clueless executives ordering 5,000 GPUs without knowing what they are, confusing China and Taiwan, and estimating the logistics as 'one or two story points.'

recent_posts.title: How startup culture normalized revenue fraud and fake metrics
recent_posts.summary: A critical look at the normalization of fraud and deception in startup culture, covering a founder caught faking revenue metrics on TrustMR to attract investors, Perplexity's alleged undisclosed paid influencer ring on X, and the broader issue of 'contracted ARR' manipulation. The piece argues that accelerator pressure (YC, a16z Speedrun) to hit aggressive ARR targets in short timeframes is incentivizing founders to cheat, gaslight investors, and prioritize Twitter clout over building real products.

recent_posts.title: How AI and bad actors are destroying the hackathon ecosystem
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares firsthand experiences judging and participating in hackathons over three months, arguing that AI and predatory company behavior have degraded the hackathon ecosystem. Key issues include: companies using hackathons to farm ideas for pivots (citing Wordware's $30M-funded event as a prime example), participants reusing winning projects across multiple hackathons to game job offers, AI making cheating nearly undetectable via vibe coding, and security failures like leaked API keys in public repos. The author contrasts bad hackathons with well-run ones like the YC browser-use hackathon, and calls for more accountability in the space.

recent_posts.title: Anthropic's Claude Mythos announcement is marketing dressed as safety concern
recent_posts.summary: A critical, comedic take on Anthropic's announcement of Claude Mythos, a new AI model they claim is too dangerous for public release. The author mocks the 245-page model card as corporate PR fanfic, questions the sincerity of Anthropic's safety concerns given that existing tools like Claude Code already enable security exploits, and ridicules the employee testimonials and model welfare assessment included in the report. The piece also calls out Anthropic's contradictory messaging around AI replacing software engineers while still actively hiring them.

recent_posts.title: How a telehealth startup allegedly used AI fake doctors to make $410M
recent_posts.summary: A commentary on Matthew Gallagher and his telehealth company Medv, which allegedly generated $410M+ in revenue using AI-created fake doctor personas to advertise weight loss drugs (GLP-1) on Facebook. The piece critiques a New York Times article that framed Gallagher as an entrepreneurial success story while glossing over the use of 800 fake AI-generated doctor accounts, FDA warning letters, a class-action lawsuit for spam violations, and the broader pattern of 30+ telehealth companies engaging in similar questionable practices. The author argues that AI is enabling ethically dubious business models that exploit vulnerable people faster than regulation can respond.

recent_posts.title: YC startup Delve accused of faking SOC 2 compliance reports for hundreds of clients
recent_posts.summary: A YC-backed startup called Delve, valued at $300M and backed by $32M in funding, is facing serious fraud allegations. An anonymous Substack report claims Delve provided fake SOC 2 compliance reports by generating pre-filled fake evidence, using Indian certification mills operating through US shell companies, and rubber-stamping audits without real security reviews. A leaked spreadsheet of ~600 customers revealed copy-pasted compliance reports. The scandal puts Delve's clients at legal risk since they signed off on fraudulent compliance documents. Delve's response was criticized as dismissive and self-promotional. The story raises broader questions about startup culture, YC's vetting process, and the compliance industry.

recent_posts.title: How apps like Pokémon Go turned players into unpaid AI training data
recent_posts.summary: Niantic's Pokémon Go secretly built a 30-billion-image AR map of the world using player scans, which is now powering food delivery robots with centimeter-level accuracy. This reveals a broader trend where apps like YouTube, Ring, and Google Maps use user interactions as free AI training data, often buried in terms of service. The author argues that the new business model isn't selling products to users — it's harvesting user behavior and content to train AI systems, with users unknowingly acting as unpaid data laborers. The piece calls for greater transparency about how user data is collected and used.

top_posts.title: How AI coding tools affect programming skills and career paths
top_posts.summary: AI coding assistants may diminish critical thinking and programming skills through overreliance, as studies show reduced problem-solving abilities compared to manual coding. The impact depends on your goals: purists who view coding as a craft should minimize AI use to maintain deep expertise, while those focused on business outcomes can leverage AI as operators. Senior engineers have the advantage of choosing either path, though many resist AI due to ego or outdated perceptions. The key tension is between skill atrophy from AI dependence versus increased productivity for delivering business value.

top_posts.title: OpenAI faces mounting competition from Google and other AI providers
top_posts.summary: OpenAI faces increasing competition as Google's Gemini gains ground, with notable users like Salesforce CEO switching platforms. The company secured a $1 billion Disney investment for Sora video generation rights while simultaneously getting Disney to issue a cease-and-desist to Google. The launch of Images 1.5 received mixed reactions, with critics noting quality issues. OpenAI no longer leads in most AI categories as competitors catch up, causing users to migrate to alternative platforms offering better models and features.

top_posts.title: Executives misunderstand Cloudflare's scale after outage
top_posts.summary: A satirical dialogue depicting non-technical executives misunderstanding the scale and importance of Cloudflare after experiencing downtime. The humor centers on their naive belief that Cloudflare is a small company that could be easily acquired or replicated, despite it serving half the internet's infrastructure needs.

top_posts.title: AWS blamed an outage on vibe coding and other signs the world has gone off the rails
top_posts.summary: A commentary-style video transcript covering a series of absurd real-world events framed as evidence we live in a simulation: the White House posting AI-generated war videos on Twitter, a viral McDonald's CEO burger review spawning a Burger King CEO clap-back, Taco Bell launching Mountain Dew Baja Blast under-eye patches, AWS blaming an outage on AI-assisted deployments (vibe coding), and McKinsey's AI platform getting hacked within 2 hours. The AWS incident is used to raise broader questions about AI as a corporate scapegoat and whether enterprise vibe coding is ready for production.
